page.text:
The natural numbers can be added but not freely subtracted: there is no
natural number equal to $3 - 5$. The integers repair this by adjoining
negative numbers. The classical construction, carried out here,
represents each integer as a difference of two naturals -- the pair
$(n, m)$ standing for $n - m$ -- and then identifies pairs that ought to
name the same difference. This is exactly a quotient by an equivalence
relation, so it draws on every earlier chapter at once: the naturals,
their addition, the Cartesian product, and the quotient of a set by a
relation.
